paragraphs: Here's what I see in this one, friend. Jesus came for rest, and a crowd got there first. He didn't send them away. Mark 6:34 says He "had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd." His plans got interrupted, and His heart went straight to the people in front of Him.

Then the disciples hand Him the practical answer: send everybody off to buy their own food (Mark 6:35-36). Jesus says, "You give them something to eat" (Mark 6:37). They count what they've got, and it's five loaves and two fish (Mark 6:38). Friend, I have stood in front of an empty cookie jar with a crowd at the door, and I would have said what they said. But look at what Jesus does with a small amount in His hands: He blesses it, breaks it, and "They all ate and were satisfied" (Mark 6:41-42).

So here's what I'm baking into you today. You don't have to have enough. You just have to bring what you've got and put it in Jesus' hands. He cares about hungry people, and He brings the disciples into His work by letting them set out what He gave. Twelve basketfuls were left over (Mark 6:43), so when your own supply looks small, bring it to Him anyway.
